title: BECE Business Studies: Book-keeping - Business Studies - Trading, Profit and Loss Account
subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The primary purpose of preparing a Trading, Profit and Loss Account at the end of a financial period is to ascertain the:
options: total cash balance in the bank
financial position of the business on a given date
gross profit and net profit of the business
arithmetical accuracy of the ledger entries
questions.explain: The **purpose of the Trading, Profit and Loss Account** is to calculate the profitability of the business. The Trading section determines the *Gross Profit/Loss*, while the Profit and Loss section determines the final *Net Profit/Loss*.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The Trading Account is specifically designed to reveal the difference between the sales revenue and the:
questions.explain:
The Trading Account matches the revenue earned from sales against the direct cost of purchasing those goods. 
$$\text{Gross Profit} = \text{Net Sales} - \text{Cost of Goods Sold (COGS)}$$
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following items is recorded on the debit side of the Trading Account?
questions.explain: The debit side of the Trading Account records the costs incurred. **Opening stock** is the first item on the debit side. *Sales* and *Closing stock* are recorded on the credit side, while *Return outwards* is deducted from Purchases on the debit side.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A trader starts the year with an Opening Stock of $₦15,000$. During the year, Purchases amount to $₦40,000$ and Closing Stock is valued at $₦10,000$. What is the Cost of Goods Sold (COGS)?
questions.explain:
The formula for calculating Cost of Goods Sold in the Trading Account is:
$$\text{COGS} = \text{Opening Stock} + \text{Purchases} - \text{Closing Stock}$$
$$\text{COGS} = ₦15,000 + ₦40,000 - ₦10,000 = ₦45,000$$
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: If a business has a Cost of Goods Sold of $₦45,000$ and total Net Sales of $₦70,000$, what is the Gross Profit for the period?
questions.explain:
Gross profit is the excess of Net Sales over the Cost of Goods Sold.
$$\text{Gross Profit} = \text{Net Sales} - \text{COGS}$$
$$\text{Gross Profit} = ₦70,000 - ₦45,000 = ₦25,000$$
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: When constructing a Profit and Loss Account, how is a Gross Profit figure transferred from the Trading Account?
options: It is debited to the Profit and Loss Account
It is credited to the Profit and Loss Account
It is subtracted from the indirect expenses
It is ignored until the Balance Sheet is prepared
questions.explain: A Gross Profit represents an income balance (credit balance). By the rules of double entry, it is brought down and **credited** to the Profit and Loss Account to serve as the main source of income to cover indirect expenses.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: All of the following are examples of indirect expenses charged to the Profit and Loss Account EXCEPT:
questions.explain: **Carriage Inwards** is the cost of transporting purchased goods into the business. It is a *direct cost* and is charged to the **Trading Account**. Items like Rent, Salaries, and Discount Allowed are indirect/operating expenses charged to the Profit and Loss Account.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: According to the rules for constructing a Simple Trading Account, to calculate the 'Net Sales', a book-keeper must deduct which of the following from the total Sales figure?
questions.explain:
**Return Inwards** (Sales Returns) represents goods sent back by customers. To find the true, actual sales revenue for the period, Return Inwards must be deducted from the gross Sales.
$$\text{Net Sales} = \text{Sales} - \text{Return Inwards}$$
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A business has Purchases totalling $₦60,000$ and goods returned to suppliers (Return Outwards) valued at $₦4,000$. What is the Net Purchases figure?
questions.explain:
Net Purchases is calculated by subtracting returns made to the supplier from the total purchases.
$$\text{Net Purchases} = \text{Purchases} - \text{Return Outwards}$$
$$\text{Net Purchases} = ₦60,000 - ₦4,000 = ₦56,000$$
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Where should the item 'Discount Received' be recorded when constructing the Profit and Loss Account?
options: On the debit side as an expense
On the debit side as a liability
On the credit side as an additional income
On the credit side as a fixed asset
questions.explain: **Discount Received** is a reduction in payment granted by a supplier. It represents a financial gain or additional income to the business, and therefore it is recorded on the **credit side** of the Profit and Loss Account.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q:
Study the figures below for a small business:
*   Gross Profit: $₦30,000$
*   Rent Paid: $₦4,000$
*   Stationery: $₦1,500$
*   Commission Received: $₦2,500$

What is the Net Profit for the period?
questions.explain:
Net Profit is calculated by adding other incomes to Gross Profit and then subtracting all indirect expenses.

1.  **Total Income** = Gross Profit + Commission Received 
    $$₦30,000 + ₦2,500 = ₦32,500$$
2.  **Total Expenses** = Rent Paid + Stationery
    $$₦4,000 + ₦1,500 = ₦5,500$$
3.  **Net Profit** = Total Income - Total Expenses
    $$₦32,500 - ₦5,500 = ₦27,000$$
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: If a Profit and Loss Account shows total expenses (debit side) of $₦45,000$ and total gross profit and incomes (credit side) of $₦38,000$, the business has made a:
questions.explain:
When the total operating expenses (debits) exceed the total incomes (credits) in the Profit and Loss Account, the result is a **Net Loss**.
$$\text{Net Loss} = ₦45,000 - ₦38,000 = ₦7,000$$
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q:
Examine the extracted balances below:

| Item | Amount (₦) |
| :--- | :--- |
| Sales | 100,000 |
| Cost of Goods Sold | 60,000 |
| Operating Expenses | 25,000 |

Using the rules of final accounts, calculate the final Net Profit.
questions.explain:
This requires a two-step calculation representing the Trading Account and the Profit & Loss Account:

**Step 1: Calculate Gross Profit (Trading Account)**
$$\text{Gross Profit} = \text{Sales} - \text{COGS}$$
$$\text{Gross Profit} = ₦100,000 - ₦60,000 = ₦40,000$$

**Step 2: Calculate Net Profit (Profit and Loss Account)**
$$\text{Net Profit} = \text{Gross Profit} - \text{Operating Expenses}$$
$$\text{Net Profit} = ₦40,000 - ₦25,000 = ₦15,000$$
